Campaigns are split at gaps of more than 30 days between reports; the campaigns below are in date order.

Campaign 2 runs from 2007-12-30 to 2008-02-11: 44.0 days span, 38 active days, dominant phase drilling.

Campaign 3 runs from 2009-03-13 to 2009-03-17: 5.0 days span, 5 active days, dominant phase workover.
Campaign 4 runs from 2010-09-20 to 2010-09-23: 4.0 days span, 4 active days, dominant phase workover.
Campaign 5 runs from 2014-11-22 to 2014-11-27: 6.0 days span, 6 active days, dominant phase workover.
Campaign 6 runs from 2016-08-14 to 2016-08-28: 15.0 days span, 15 active days, dominant phase plug abandon.
Campaign 7 runs from 2016-10-19 to 2016-10-20: 2.0 days span, 2 active days, dominant phase plug abandon.
Rates below are averages over all time coded drilling -- drill, not on-bottom rates of penetration.

Section 2 is an 8.5 in section from 2007-06-17 to 2007-07-04, from 258.0 m to 1353.0 m measured depth, with 1353.0 m true vertical depth at section end, 1095.0 m of new hole and an average rate of 9.38 m/h while coded drilling.

Section 3 is a 26.0 in section from 2007-07-05 to 2007-07-14, from 258.0 m to 1369.0 m measured depth, with 1344.0 m true vertical depth at section end, 16.0 m of new hole and an average rate of 0.13 m/h while coded drilling.

Section 5 is a 17.5 in section from 2007-07-21 to 2007-08-10, from 1372.0 m to 2572.5 m measured depth, with 2481.5 m true vertical depth at section end, 1203.5 m of new hole and an average rate of 6.12 m/h while coded drilling.

Sections 8 to 24 have no hole size in the tools (source unknown) and drilled no new hole. They run from 2007-08-26 (section 8) through completion, workover and plug-and-abandon work. Section 24, the plug-and-abandon section, runs from 2016-08-14 to 2016-10-20 with 356.5 activity hours.

Section 2 sets no casing. Section 3 starts below the 251.0 m shoe and sets casing with its shoe at 1357.0 m.
Section 4 and section 5 start below the 1357.0 m shoe and set no casing.
Section 6 starts below the 1357.0 m shoe and sets casing with its shoe at 3113.0 m.

Primary lost time is 195.75 hours, 5.2% of the wellbore's activity time. By section, it is 77.25 hours in section 2 (17.88% of section activity), 8.75 hours in section 3 (3.65%) and 13.25 hours in section 6 (5.02%).

Section 24 adds 25.75 hours (7.22%) of primary lost time, and sections 4, 5, 7, 10, 13, 15 and 19 add 2.25 hours (1.56%), 2.75 hours (0.55%), 1.5 hours (1.56%), 0.5 hours (0.23%), 1.0 hours (1.57%), 1.5 hours (0.48%) and 1.0 hours (1.45%) respectively.

By cause, primary lost time is 72.0 hours of drilling -- wait, 59.25 hours of interruption -- repair, 58.0 hours of interruption -- waiting on weather, 2.25 hours of interruption -- rig up/down, 2.25 hours of interruption -- well control and 2.0 hours of interruption -- fish.

Possible lost time is reported separately and is not added to the primary figures. The PRS repairs ran until 2008-01-11, when slip repairs took 5.25 hours of possible time.

claims.value: Indication of leakage from tie-back casing to B-annulus confirmed.

sentences.text: On 2008-01-14 a tie-back pressure test confirmed a leak from the tie-back casing into the B-annulus; the report reads: "Indication of leakage from tie-back casing to B-annulus confirmed."
On 2008-01-16 the crew waited 9.5 hours for instructions from onshore, and then 4.0 hours on weather (primary) before running the perforating guns.
On 2008-01-17 the perforating gun run was stopped while running in hole for discussion of testing requirements, a stop of 3.25 hours, and the guns were then pulled out of hole.

On 2008-01-19 high winds stopped work for 6.0 hours of weather wait (primary), and a further 2.25 hours were coded interruption -- well control (primary) while the aft PRS drag chain was inspected and the rig floor was barricaded.
On 2016-08-17 the landing string was overtorqued with the wrong tong setting, damaging a pup joint and the running tool, a 1.0 hour primary repair.
On 2016-08-17 the subsurface safety valve (DHSV) would not communicate and pressure was trapped below it; the crew spent 1.0 hour of primary repair on the pressure-up and bleed sequence.
On 2016-08-18 the tubing hanger was pulled free after 1.0 hour of work, and a trip-tank gain showed that the seals had pulled out of the PBR.
On 2016-08-19 a loose stand in the derrick was recovered and the elevators were found damaged and changed out, a 2.0 hour primary fish.
On 2016-08-19 an increase in gas returns during circulation before the cement plug was handled through the gas traps, a 0.75 hour activity.

claims.value: The connection backed out from X-over

sentences.text: On 2016-08-20 the tie-back adapter connection backed out below the rotary and the torque-tool BHA was left in the hole; the report reads: "The connection backed out from X-over".
The loss of the BHA was confirmed on 2016-08-21 after 1.5 hours of tie-back adapter work, and the fish was latched on the same day after 1.0 hour.
On 2016-08-21 the replacement crossover that arrived was right-hand rather than left-hand, a 0.75 hour primary repair; the report reads "it was right hand X-over".
The perforating guns fired on 2016-08-21 in a 0.5 hour operation, after which the well took losses and gas that circulation brought under control.

claims.value: Observed bubbling inside drill string and in the riser, smell of gas.

sentences.text: On 2016-08-22 the casing was cut in 1.0 hour, and a flow check after the cut showed a gain and bubbling in the drill string and riser over 1.25 hours; the report reads "Observed bubbling inside drill string and in the riser, smell of gas."
The tie-back adapter did not release after 4.0 hours of rig-tong pulls on 2016-08-22; the report reads "Tieback adapter did not release."

The Sodir completion date of 2007-08-27 marks the end of drilling, while the last report on 2016-10-20 is later because completion work began with campaign 2 on 2007-12-30, followed by workovers in campaigns 3 to 5 and plug and abandonment in campaigns 6 and 7. The tools record no technical sidetrack for this wellbore.

Put weather limits and a pipe-handling wind plan in place before the next completion: the first FWD PRS damage on 2008-01-04 led to 14.25 hours of possible time, and weather waits total 58.0 hours of primary time on this well.
Pressure-test the tie-back and B-annulus before running further completion equipment: the leak was confirmed on 2008-01-14, and the crew then waited 9.5 hours for instructions on 2008-01-16.
Act early when drilling stalls: the 26.0 in section 3 made 16.0 m of new hole at an average 0.13 m/h over 125.25 drilling hours.

Verify make-up torque and thread handedness before running landing strings and X-overs: the overtorque on 2016-08-17 cost 1.0 hour of primary repair and the wrong-hand crossover on 2016-08-21 cost 0.75 hour.
Inspect elevators and stands before lifting: the loose stand on 2016-08-19 led to 2.0 hours of primary fish time with damaged elevators.
Plan gas handling for cement-plug jobs: the gas increase on 2016-08-19 took 0.75 hour to route through the gas traps before cementing.

row.comments: Held toolbox talk prior to making up 7" x 9 5/8" x 10 3/4" clean out string.

Waiting on improved weather conditions to perform repair on FWD PRS. Wind speed 60 knots.

Meanwhile :
-Performed general maintenance on aft IR
-Performed general housekeeping and cleaning in moonpool, rigfloor, shakers and pitroom
-Put protectors on pin end of 7" tubing laid out on deck
Repaired on PS-21 slips. Released slips. Exchanged PS-21 with PS-30 slips.

Pressured up well to 200 bar and observed annulus pressure increase to 25 bar. Pressure fell on well and increased on annulus :

5 min : well; 2,4 bar drop / annulus; 3 bar cummulative increase
10 min : well; 4,6 bar drop / annulus; 6 bar cummulative increase
15 min : well; 6,4 bar drop / annulus; 9 bar cummulative increase
20 min : well; 7,5 bar drop / annulus; 11 bar cummulative increase

Indication of leakage from tie-back casing to B-annulus confirmed. Leakage rate with closed annulus at approx 200 bar - 2,5 l/min.

Waited for instuctions from town.

Meanwhile :
-Pressure tested safety valves
-Performed manitenance on rotary table lock
-Performed general housekeeping and PM's on drillfloor
-Removed BOP carrier from BOP
Recieved instruction from town to run guns. Waited on weather due to high winds, cranes down. Meanwhile rigged up casing tong, dressed PS-21 slips for 4 1/2" and dressed BX elevator with 5" inserts.
Stopped RIH. Discussed testing requirements and further plans for F-12 with town.
Waited on weather due to high winds up to 72 knop and danger for people to be present in well head module.

Waited on weather due to high winds up to 60 knop and danger for people to be present in well head module.

Meanwhile inspected AFT PRS and found damage on drag chain. Barried off rig floor.

Overtorqued connection between THRT and first joint due to wrong tong setting. 
Troubleshoot, broke out and inspected treads. Damaged. L/D damaged pup joint and THRT

Connected another hydraulic pump to control line, applied 520bar to control line. Started pressuring up tubing while monitoring gauge on the hydraulic pump for indications of DHSV sleeve movement. 
Observed DHSV equalized and opened at 146 bar and stop pressuring up at 152bar. No indication of DHSV sleeve movement. Bled off pressure, volume returned 60 liters. 152bar trapped below DHSV

Installed circulating swedge for TDS. M/U TDS and unlock tubing hanger. 
Pull tubing hanger free with 185t hook load (15ton overpull). Observed drop in Trip tank indicating that A-annulus was not 100% full. Waited for trip tank level to stabilize, total of 2 m3 lost

Observed loose stand in derrick. Held TBT, recovered stand using forward PRS and returned to TDS. Held stand w/ aft PRS to lower down TDS to be able to inspect elevators. Elevators found to be damaged. Changed out elevators to spare set. 
Performed drops check of aft PRS before continuing with operation.
M/U TDS and staged up pump rate to 3700 l/min - 178 bar. Observed increase in gas returns to 10%, stopped pump and lined up returns through gas traps
POOH from 141,5m, visually checked all connections. When reached end of last 5,5in HWDP stand observed no BHA. The connection backed out from X-over
RIH w/ DP from surface to 137 m. M/U TDS and latched on to fish. POOH from to surface. L/D torque tool
Left hand X-over arrived on the rig. Inspected and discovered it was right hand X-over. Evaluated situation. Meanwhile performed hydraulic test on BX4.

Pumped down ball with 160 l/min, sheared ball seat at 150 bar. Indication of guns firing (sound, vibration on surface). Top shot at 144,5m, bottom shot at 147,5m. Continued pumping with 150 l/min until returns, increased to 770 l/min, observed slight gain of 500ltr and then losses of 60m3/hr. Pumped 1,5 times btms up, gas observed and still on losses

Continued RIH w/ torque tool. Engaged to tie-back adapter. Marked pipe. Attempted to back out adapter counter clockwise. Applied 25kNm in steps before pipe started to rotate. Than rotated free at 2kNm. Measured distance 1,5in after 5 turns. POOH. Observed no torque tool/X/over on the drill pipe - left in hole
Attached ropes to rig tong, trapped 26kNm with TDS. Pulled w/ rig tong up to 75kNm on the string. Tieback adapter did not release. Meanwhile discussed with onshore organization way forward

M/U TDS. Positioned cutters to cutting depth of 887m. Up/down weights 97t/90t, took parameters 75rpm - 4-7kNM, 300l/min - 18bar, 400l/min - 35bar, 500l/min - 61bar. Cut csg at 887m w/ 300l/min - 21bar, 80rpm - 8-12kNm. Measured gap of more than 2.7m

Flowchecked well. Observed instant gain of 300l, then loss of 3m3/hour. Then losses went to 0. Observed bubbling inside drill string and in the riser, smell of gas. M/U TDS to string and observed increase in trip tank
